claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 17 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 17 and in the 20-week extension period
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning a new eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child or children.

**How old is/are your child/children?**

To help determine your eligibility, I need to know:
- The age(s) of the child/children you're claiming for
- Whether any are 16-19 and in education or training

Please tell me:
1. How many children are you enquiring about?
2. What are their ages?

This will help me understand which path of the eligibility rules applies to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about one child - my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing that context! Let me get the detailed information for this age group.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Since Alex is 17 years old, he falls into the 16-19 age group. Now I need to check his education status.

**Is Alex currently in education or training?**

By "in education or training," I mean:
- Is he at school (secondary school, sixth form, college)?
- Is he on an apprenticeship or other accredited training programme?
- Is he in any other full-time education/training course?

Or has he recently left education (within the last 20 weeks)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He recently left education actually. He finished school but he's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex recently left education, let me check what extension eligibility rules apply in his situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! This is very helpful. I can see that there's a 20-week extension available if Alex has recently left education and registered with a qualifying service.

**Let me ask you a couple of important questions:**

1. **When exactly did Alex finish school?** (I need to know if it's been within the last 20 weeks)

2. **Is he registered with a qualifying service?** The help text indicates that he needs to be registered with one of these services to qualify for the extension:
   - Government careers service
   - Connexions
   - Armed services

You mentioned he's signed up with the local careers service - is that a government careers service?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's registered with the government careers service - they've been helping him look at different options. He left school about 2 months ago, so it's been around 8 or 9 weeks now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! This is very positive information for Alex's eligibility. Let me confirm:

- ✓ Alex left school approximately 8-9 weeks ago (well within the 20-week extension period)
- ✓ He is registered with the government careers service (a qualifying service)

This means Alex qualifies for the 20-week extension! Now I need to check one more important requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check one more thing about Alex's work situation.

**Is Alex working?** Specifically:
- Is he working less than 24 hours per week, or
- Is he not in paid work at all?

(The rule is that children aged 16+ cannot work 24 or more hours per week and still qualify for Child Benefit, unless they're in approved education or training - which Alex isn't currently in, though he's in the extension period.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now. He's just been focusing on figuring out his next steps with the careers service.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's another positive step. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is receiving any benefits in his own right.

**Is Alex receiving any of the following benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

Or is he not claiming any of these benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own right.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me check the next requirement about apprenticeships.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check if Alex is in any apprenticeships.

**Is Alex in any apprenticeship programme?**

If so, the rules vary by region:
- **England**: All types of apprenticeships (Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, Degree) would disqualify him
- **Scotland**: Modern Apprenticeships would disqualify him
- **Wales**: Foundation Apprenticeships are approved (he'd still qualify), but other apprenticeships would disqualify him

Is he in any apprenticeship, and if so, which region are you in and what type?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started any apprenticeship. As I mentioned, he's just working with the careers service to figure out what he wants to do.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now I need to check the residency requirements for you as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. Child Benefit has specific residency requirements, and there are several paths that can qualify you.

**Which of the following applies to your situation:**

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the most common route)

Or, if you don't normally live in the UK:

2. Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
3. Do you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme? (If so, there are further requirements depending on your circumstances - working, seeking work, studying, etc.)
4. Are you a Crown servant living abroad in a qualifying country?

Which path applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That satisfies the residency requirement. Now I need to check one more important aspect: your responsibility for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. You've already mentioned he lives at home with you, but let me confirm:

**Which of the following applies:**

1. **Do you live with Alex?** (You mentioned he lives at home with you, so this should be yes)

Or if not living together:

2. Are you contributing to Alex's upkeep? (This could include paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents - at least the equivalent value of Child Benefit)

3. Are you paying maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement?

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like you live with Alex, so you should meet this requirement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me check if there are any other claimants for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or have agreed to claim for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Has anyone else claimed him?
- Or are you the only person claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm the only one. Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Now let me check the final requirement about where Alex is located.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation for any special circumstances.

**Is Alex:**
- In hospital?
- In care (residential/institutional care)?
- Being fostered?
- Or living normally at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me check the final requirement about council payments.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! We're almost at the end. Just one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the council paying for his housing, food, or any other costs of keeping him?
- Or are you fully responsible for his upkeep without council financial support?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance. I'm fully responsible for his upkeep.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! I have all the information I need. Let me now provide you with the eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

### Summary of Your Situation:

**Child:** Alex (17 years old)

**Result:** ✅ **ELIGIBLE**

---

### Why You're Eligible:

1. **Age & Education Status:** Although Alex has left school, he qualifies for the **20-week extension** because he has registered with the government careers service within the required timeframe (8-9 weeks ago).

2. **Work Status:** He is not working full-time (0 hours per week - well under the 24-hour limit).

3. **Benefits:** He is not receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in his own right.

4. **Apprenticeship:** He is not in any disqualifying apprenticeship.

5. **Your Residency:** You are normally resident in the UK.

6. **Responsibility:** You live with Alex and are fully responsible for his upkeep - you're the sole claimant.

7. **Living Situation:** Alex is living normally at home with you.

8. **Council Support:** The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance.

---

### What Happens Next:

You can now **claim Child Benefit for Alex**. Here are the important points to remember:

- **Time Limit:** The 20-week extension will end when Alex either:
  - Completes 20 weeks from leaving education, OR
  - Turns 18 (whichever comes first)
  
  After that time, eligibility will depend on whether he enters approved education/training or another qualifying circumstance.

- **How to Claim:** Visit [gov.uk/child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit) to apply online or contact HMRC.

- **Keep Records:** Keep records of Alex's registration with the careers service in case you need to evidence his eligibility.

Congratulations! You have a strong case for eligibility. Good luck with your application!

Within this extension period, he meets all other eligibility requirements: (1) He is not working full-time (working 0 hours per week, well under the 24-hour threshold); (2) He is not receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in his own right; (3) He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (4) You are his parent, normally resident in the UK; (5) You live with Alex and are responsible for his upkeep; (6) You are the only claimant for Alex; (7) Alex is living normally at home with you; and (8) The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are satisfied.

You can proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex."
